column1: # The fuzzy core's rule, as rows its implementations replay.
# Rust core, and noctua-design's matcher replays the same rows once the
# interface brings it to this rule. A row is a claim about the rule, so a change
# to the rule changes a row in the same edit, and a row nobody can explain is a
# defect in the rule or in the row.
# Tab-separated, one row per line; a line opening with # is a comment, and a
#   fold    TEXT    FOLDED          each character of TEXT folds to the one at its index in FOLDED
#   words   QUERY   WORDS           the words of QUERY, folded, joined by |, or - for none
#   match   QUERY   ITEM    HITS    how QUERY matches one item, or - when it does not
#   order   QUERY   ITEMS   ORDER   the indices QUERY finds among ITEMS, best first, joined by ;, or - for none
# An ITEM is its fields joined by |, each a name unless it opens with tag: and
# ITEMS are items joined by ;. HITS hold one hit per word of the query, in the
# order the words were typed, joined by |: the index of the field the word
# matched and a colon, left out for the first field, then its positions as
# indices and inclusive ranges joined by commas. A position is a character's
# index in the field's own text, separators counted.
# A backslash, u and a hexadecimal code point in braces writes any character,
# and is how a row holds a tab, an invisible character, a space at the edge of a
# column, or one of | ; and the backslash itself. No other backslash is read.
# The letters are kept to those whose case and decomposition every Unicode
# version a browser or a system ships agrees on.
# One character to one character: lower case first, then the base letter.
# A capital whose lower case is two characters as a string is one here.
# A letter with no decomposition is not folded to a letter it resembles.
# Title case and the two-letter capitals lower case to their small forms.
# A Hangul syllable keeps itself: folded, one syllable would find every syllable
# A letter outside the basic plane folds like any other.
# A query is split at spaces, and a separator inside a word is dropped.
# Every word must match, each in its own field, and words may share characters.
# A separator is skipped in the field and dropped in the query.
# A run opening a word beats an earlier run inside one, every occurrence weighed.
# Scattered: more word starts, then more adjacent characters, then earlier.
# A one-letter word matches wherever its letter is.
# Order is required, and every character.
# A Hangul syllable finds itself and not the syllables sharing its consonant.
# A word reports the field it matched, and the field it matched best.
# At an equal tier a name beats a tag, wherever each begins; a tier beats a name.
# The tier, then the role, then starts, adjacent characters, earliness and shortness.
# A query in Portuguese finds through a Portuguese synonym, one in English through the English name.
